friends.nshan.name: Nshan
friends.nshan.lines.0: Hi, I'm Nshan! Let's see what we're up to now.
friends.nshan.lines.1: I play on this farm too. Here's your quest.
friends.nshan.lines.2: One step at a time. No need to rush.
friends.erik.name: Erik
friends.erik.lines.0: I'm Erik. I got stuck here too, and here's what helped me.
friends.erik.lines.1: Never give up, just like Ronaldo! Listen.
friends.erik.lines.2: Here's a little hint. The rest is up to you.
starterCode:
// Write your code here.
// Bridgy will show you how.
intro.0.text: Hi there! I'm Bridgy, the robot farmer of this farm. I'm so happy you came!
intro.1.text: My little helper, the drone, works on the farm. But the drone can't do anything on its own. Someone has to tell it what to do.
intro.2.text: That's what code is for: commands written in JavaScript. You write code in the code window, and the green ▶ "Run" button runs it.
intro.3.text: Every command has three parts: first the name, then parentheses (), and a semicolon ; at the end. For example, this command makes the drone do a flip:
intro.4.text: The command for gathering wheat is called gather. Command names in code use only English letters and have no spaces.
intro.5.text: Now it's your turn! In the code window, under the comment lines, write the command to gather wheat: the name, () and ;. Then press ▶. If you make a mistake, I'll help.
lessons.Music.0.text: Beep-boop, the drone can play music now! playNote() plays notes with a piano sound, and the drone hops while it plays.
lessons.Music.1.text: First comes the note, then how many beats it lasts (one beat is half a second):
lessons.Music.2.text: Notes.Rest is silence. You can also write "C#4" or "Bb3" for pitches in different octaves. A list of notes plays a chord. Choose the tempo with the third number, like playNote(Notes.C, 1, 100). Find the details on the command's page, and try your favorite tune!
lessons.Loops.0.text: You unlocked while: the loop! A loop runs the same commands again and again, so you don't have to press ▶ every time.
lessons.Loops.1.text: A while loop looks like this:
lessons.Loops.2.text: while means "as long as." Inside the parentheses we write a condition. As long as it's true, the commands inside the curly braces { } keep repeating.
lessons.Loops.3.text: If the condition is just true, the loop repeats forever. For example, with this code the drone does flips forever:
lessons.Loops.4.text: To stop an endless loop, press the "Stop" button. And don't forget: every { needs a } to close it.
lessons.Loops.5.text: Let's check: did you get it? What will this code do?
lessons.Loops.5.quiz.answers.0: Two flips, and then it stops
lessons.Loops.5.quiz.answers.2: Nothing, because the code is wrong
lessons.Loops.5.quiz.right: Correct! true is always true, so the loop never ends. Each time around, the drone does two flips.
lessons.Loops.5.quiz.wrong: Not quite. Remember: true means "always," and the commands inside { } repeat. Try again.
lessons.Expand.0.text: The farm got bigger! Now the drone can move with go().
lessons.Expand.1.text: Inside the parentheses of go(), write a direction: Up, Down, Right or Left. For example, one tile to the left:
lessons.Expand.2.text: If the drone goes past the edge of the farm, it pops up on the other side. That way it can keep going around forever.
lessons.Expand.3.text: You can put several commands inside a loop. They run one after another, from top to bottom. For example: a flip, then one step left, and so on forever:
lessons.Plant.0.text: Now you can plant! sow() plants something under the drone. Inside the parentheses, write which plant, for example Plants.Rosehip. Rosehips give wood.
lessons.Plant.1.text: But a rosehip takes a few seconds to grow. If you gather it before it's ripe, you get nothing. So first you need to check. That's what if is for.
lessons.Plant.2.text: if does just what it says: it runs the commands only if the condition is true:
lessons.Plant.3.text: isRipe() answers true (yes, it's ripe) or false (no). You can use it as the condition of an if. And else ("otherwise") runs when the condition isn't true:
lessons.Plant.4.text: Read it like this: "If it's ripe, do a flip. Otherwise, go right."
lessons.Plant.5.text: whatsHere() tells you what's growing under the drone. You can compare its answer with ==, for example, to check if there's a rosehip under the drone:
lessons.Plant.6.text: Let's check. The rosehip isn't ripe yet. What will the drone do with this code?
lessons.Plant.6.quiz.right: Correct! isRipe() is false, so the if part is skipped and the else part runs.
lessons.Plant.6.quiz.wrong: Nope. The rosehip isn't ripe, so isRipe() is false. Then only the else part runs. Try again.
lessons.Hats.0.text: Hats! The drone can change its hat with wearHat(). The hats live in the Hats group:
lessons.Hats.1.text: There are Blue, Green, Red and Purple hats, and the plain straw hat is Straw. Pick your favorite color!
lessons.Carrots.0.text: Eggplants (Plants.Eggplant)! But eggplants only grow in plowed soil.
lessons.Carrots.1.text: plow() plows the ground under the drone: meadow turns into plowed soil. Careful: if you plow it again, it turns back into meadow.
lessons.Carrots.2.text: soilType() tells you what's under the drone: Soils.Meadow (meadow) or Soils.Field (plowed soil).
lessons.Carrots.3.text: Eggplants grow from seeds (Goods.Seeds). Your first seeds are hiding in the wheat: gather wheat, and about 1 stalk in 20 will drop a seed.
lessons.Carrots.4.text: Every eggplant you gather gives back 1 to 3 seeds, so you get more and more seeds. But if you gather an eggplant before it's ripe, the seed is lost too. count(Goods.Seeds) tells you how many seeds you have.
lessons.Carrots.5.text: Tip: first plow every tile once, then gather and replant inside a loop. Think: which commands do you need just once, and which go inside the loop?
lessons.Debug.0.text: say() writes in the console, under the code window. It helps you see what's going on in your code.
lessons.Debug.1.text: Text goes inside quotes: "like this". Numbers go without quotes. You can also show a variable or a command's answer:
lessons.Debug.2.text: In real JavaScript, console.log() does the same thing. Both work here, so pick the one you like:
lessons.Debug.3.text: alert() shows text in a window, and the code waits until you press "OK". It's handy when you want to stop and take a look:
lessons.Debug.4.text: Let's check. What will this code say?
lessons.Debug.4.quiz.right: Correct! say(a) shows what's in box a right now, and that's 8.
lessons.Debug.4.quiz.wrong: Not quite. say(a) doesn't show the letter a, it shows what's inside the box. And what did we put in last? Try again.
lessons.Operators.0.text: Now the drone can do math! + adds, - subtracts, * multiplies, / divides, and % gives the remainder of a division.
lessons.Operators.1.text: You can also compare. The answer is always true or false:
lessons.Operators.1.code:
5 == 5    // equal
5 != 3    // not equal
2 < 7     // less than
9 >= 9    // greater than or equal
lessons.Operators.2.text: Now you can count with a variable. This loop repeats as long as flips is less than 3, and each time around flips goes up by 1:
lessons.Operators.3.text: You can write the same thing shorter with a for loop. Its parentheses hold three parts: the start, the condition and the step (i++ means i = i + 1):
lessons.Operators.4.text: Read it like this: "i starts at 0. As long as i < 3, do a flip and add 1 to i." So the drone does 3 flips: i = 0, 1, 2.
lessons.Operators.5.text: You can join conditions: && ("and": both are true), || ("or": at least one is true), ! ("not": flips the answer). And careful: == compares, but a single = puts a value into a box.
lessons.Operators.6.text: Let's check. How many times will the drone go right?
lessons.Operators.6.quiz.right: Correct! i is 0, then 2, then 4, and at 6 the condition is already false. So: 3 times.
lessons.Operators.6.quiz.wrong: Not quite. Notice that i goes up by 2 each time. Write down the values of i: 0, 2, … Try again.
lessons.Senses.0.text: Now the drone knows where it is! posX() is the column (left to right), and posY() is the row (bottom to top). We count from 0.
lessons.Senses.1.text: farmSize() is the size of the farm (3 on a 3×3 farm), and count() tells you how much of something you have:
lessons.Senses.2.text: Think: on a 3×3 farm, the rightmost column is number 2, not 3, because we count from 0. So the last column is farmSize() - 1.
lessons.Variables.0.text: A variable is a box where we keep a value. The box has a name, and later we use that name to get the value back. You make a variable with the word let:
lessons.Variables.1.text: Now the box called side holds Right. You can write the box's name anywhere a direction goes:
lessons.Variables.2.text: The = sign puts a new value into the box, and the old one is forgotten. You only write let the first time:
lessons.Variables.3.text: A variable made with const can't be changed later. It's handy for values that never change:
lessons.Variables.4.text: A variable can also hold a number or some text. You'll learn to do math with numbers soon, with the "1 + 1" research.
lessons.Variables.5.text: Let's check. Which way will the drone go?
lessons.Variables.5.quiz.right: Correct! A box only ever holds its last value. Right was replaced by Left, so the drone goes left.
lessons.Variables.5.quiz.wrong: Not quite. When we put a new value into the box, the old one is forgotten. Which one went in last? Try again.
lessons.Functions.0.text: Now you can make your own commands: functions! A function is a piece of code with a name.
lessons.Functions.1.text: You make a function with the word function:
lessons.Functions.2.text: Making a function doesn't run it yet. It only runs when you call it by its name with parentheses:
lessons.Functions.3.text: A function can take values (parameters) and give back an answer with return:
lessons.Functions.4.text: Let's check. What will this code say?
lessons.Functions.4.quiz.wrong: Not quite. First work out what sum(2, 3) gives back, then multiply it by 10. Try again.
lessons.Lists.0.text: A list (also called an array) is several values in one variable. You write it in square brackets:
lessons.Lists.1.text: The items are numbered from 0: plants[0] is the first one. plants.length is how many items there are, and push() adds a new item at the end:
lessons.Lists.2.text: A for…of loop goes through every item of a list, one by one:
lessons.Lists.3.text: Let's check. What will this code say?
lessons.Lists.3.quiz.right: Correct! t[1] is 8 (numbering starts at 0), and after push, length is 4. 8 + 4 = 12.
lessons.Lists.3.quiz.wrong: Not quite. Remember: numbering starts at 0, and push adds one more item. Try again.
lessons.Objects.0.text: An object keeps values by name (by key). We get a value with a dot:
lessons.Objects.1.text: A Map is like an object, but its key can be any value. A Set keeps values without repeats:
lessons.Objects.2.text: Let's check. What will this code say?
lessons.Objects.2.quiz.wrong: Not quite. On the second line, p.eggplant gets a new value: p.eggplant + p.watermelon. Try again.
lessons.Trees.0.text: Apricot trees (Plants.ApricotTree)! An apricot tree grows slower than a rosehip, but every harvest gives 5 wood.
lessons.Trees.1.text: An apricot tree doesn't disappear when you gather it. It gives a harvest three times, and the second and third ones ripen faster, because the tree is already big.
lessons.Trees.2.text: scan() tells you how many harvests the tree has left: 3, 2 or 1. After the last one, the tree gets old and disappears, and you need to plant a new one:
lessons.Trees.3.text: Think: when do you need to plant a new apricot tree? If you call sow() while the tree is still standing, nothing happens. So before gathering, use scan() to find out: is this the last harvest?
lessons.Mulberry.0.text: A mulberry tree (Plants.MulberryTree)! It gives 6 wood, and after you gather it, you have to plant a new one, just like a rosehip.
lessons.Mulberry.1.text: But mulberry trees love bees, and bees live near ripe rosehips. If there's a ripe rosehip next to the mulberry tree (above, below, right or left) when you gather it, you get double the wood.
lessons.Mulberry.2.text: So both the spot and the order matter. If you gather the rosehip first, the bees fly away. Think: how should you place the mulberry trees and rosehips, and which one should you gather first?
lessons.Pumpkins.0.text: Watermelons (Plants.Watermelon)! A watermelon grows in plowed soil, and planting one costs an eggplant.
lessons.Pumpkins.1.text: Watermelons are sneaky: from the outside you can't tell if one is sweet. isRipe() only tells you it's done growing. scan() measures the sweetness, from 0 to 100:
lessons.Pumpkins.2.text: Once it's done growing, a watermelon gets sweet in about 6 seconds. Gather it when the sweetness is 80 or more, and you'll get the whole harvest. Gather it earlier, and it's still green and gives nothing.
lessons.Pumpkins.3.text: But don't wait too long! About 12 seconds after it hits 100, the watermelon rots (Plants.RottenWatermelon). You can plant a new one where the rotten one was.
lessons.Pumpkins.4.text: We compare numbers with >= ("greater than or equal") and <= ("less than or equal"). Think: how do you say "if the sweetness is at least 80" with if? And how many watermelons can you gather before the first one rots?
lessons.Pumpkins.5.text: Let's check. The watermelon's sweetness is exactly 80. What will the drone do with this code?
lessons.Pumpkins.5.quiz.right: Correct! 80 isn't greater than 80, so the condition is false and the else part runs. To say "80 or more," you need the >= sign.
lessons.Pumpkins.5.quiz.wrong: Not quite. > means "strictly greater." Is 80 greater than 80? Try again.
lessons.YellowMelon.0.text: A yellow watermelon (Plants.YellowMelon)! It never rots and has no sweetness, but it has a different trick: tendrils, thin curly shoots that creep across the ground.
lessons.YellowMelon.1.text: Every few seconds, each ripe yellow watermelon sends a tendril to an empty plowed tile next to it, and a new watermelon grows there, for free. That way one watermelon turns into a whole field.
lessons.YellowMelon.2.text: One gather() collects all the ripe yellow watermelons that touch each other. n of them give n × n: 3 give 9, and 10 give a whole 100!
lessons.YellowMelon.3.text: So here's the question: when should you gather? Gather early, and the field is small. Wait, and it's bigger, but time keeps ticking. And remember: tendrils only go onto empty plowed soil.
lessons.SquareMelon.0.text: A square watermelon (Plants.SquareMelon)! These love to stick together.
lessons.SquareMelon.1.text: If ripe square watermelons side by side make a square, they join into one giant. A 2×2 giant gives 8 watermelons instead of 4, and a 3×3 one gives 27 instead of 9. That's n × n × n.
lessons.SquareMelon.2.text: To gather a giant, one gather() on any of its tiles is enough. But if you gather one watermelon before the others are ripe, the giant won't appear.
lessons.SquareMelon.3.text: Think: how can you plant a perfect square with two for loops (one inside the other), and how do you know they're all ripe?
lessons.Import.0.text: Now your files can help each other! In one file, write export before a function, and the other files can use it:
lessons.Import.1.text: …and in another file, bring it in with import and use it:
lessons.Import.2.text: The file name goes in quotes, and the function names go in curly braces. To make a new file, press the "+" button next to the files.
lessons.Import.3.text: Let's check. The main file says: import { sowRow } from "utils";. What does the utils file need for this to work?
lessons.Import.3.quiz.right: Correct! The function has to be exported, so other files can import it.
lessons.Import.3.quiz.wrong: Not quite. The file has to "send out" (export) the function, so the others can "bring it in" (import). Try again.
lessons.Mushrooms.0.text: Mushrooms! A mushroom gives magic dust, but it's very sneaky. A ripe mushroom hides either on the right or on the left, so you have to tell gather() which side to look:
lessons.Mushrooms.1.text: If you look on the wrong side, the mushroom runs off and there's no harvest. And it remembers your last choices. If you always look on the same side, or take turns (right, left, right, left), it'll soon catch on and run away every time.
lessons.Mushrooms.2.text: When can't the mushroom guess your choice?
lessons.Mushrooms.2.quiz.answers.1: If I take turns: Right, Left, Right, Left
lessons.Mushrooms.2.quiz.answers.2: If I pick at random every time
lessons.Mushrooms.2.quiz.right: Correct! A random choice can't be guessed. That way about half the mushrooms are yours. Now think: how do you write that with Math.random()?
lessons.Mushrooms.2.quiz.wrong: Not quite. The mushroom learns anything that repeats. Try again.
lessons.Utilities.0.text: Math has lots of handy functions:
lessons.Utilities.0.code:
say(Math.floor(3.7));   // 3 (rounds down)
say(Math.max(4, 9));    // 9 (the biggest)
say(Math.abs(-5));      // 5 (no minus)
lessons.Utilities.1.text: And Math.random() gives you a new random number from 0 to 1 every time (for example, 0.37).
lessons.Utilities.2.text: To get a random whole number, put them together. For example, 0, 1 or 2:
lessons.Utilities.3.text: Let's check. What will this code say?
lessons.Utilities.3.quiz.right: Correct! Math.floor(2.9) is 2, and the bigger of 2 and 1 is 2.
lessons.Utilities.3.quiz.wrong: Not quite. First work out the inside part, Math.floor(2.9), then Math.max. Try again.
lessons.SetSpeed.0.text: speed() can slow the drone down, so you have time to watch every step. speed(0.5) is half speed, speed(1) is normal.
lessons.Timing.0.text: time() is the game time in seconds. It helps you measure how fast your code is:
lessons.Costs.0.text: costOf() tells you the price of the next level of a research, and level() tells you its current level:
lessons.AutoUnlock.0.text: With research(), your code can buy research all by itself. It answers true if the purchase worked:
lessons.Watering.0.text: Water! Now you get one bucket of water (Goods.Water) every 10 seconds.
lessons.Watering.1.text: use(Goods.Water) waters the soil under the drone. In wet soil, plants grow up to 5 times faster.
lessons.Watering.2.text: waterLevel() tells you how wet the soil is: from 0 (dry) to 1 (very wet). Water dries up over time. Think: how can you use if to water only dry soil?
lessons.Calendar.0.text: The Calendar! Our farm has seasons: spring, summer, autumn and winter. Each season lasts 15 minutes and is the same for every student. The TV button at the top of the farm shows the season, the weather and today's luck.
lessons.Calendar.1.text: Every plant has a favorite season. In that season it grows twice as fast, and in the other seasons only half as fast. For example, watermelons love autumn, and pomegranates love summer. In winter, the water in the soil is ice and doesn't help the plants.
lessons.Calendar.2.text: season() tells you which season it is now: Seasons.Spring, Seasons.Summer, Seasons.Autumn or Seasons.Winter. Compare it with if, and your code will do the right thing in every season:
lessons.Calendar.3.text: The weather changes every 5 minutes: sun, rain (waters every tile and every pond), storm (lightning charges a plant: 3 times the harvest), heat (water dries up fast) and snow. weather() tells you the weather now, and nextWeather() the next one. And in winter and in the rain, the ponds have fish you can't catch at any other time.
lessons.Calendar.4.text: A question: it's raining. Should your code use water right now?
lessons.Calendar.4.quiz.answers.0: Yes, the more water the better
lessons.Calendar.4.quiz.answers.1: No, the rain already waters every tile
lessons.Calendar.4.quiz.right: Correct! Save your water when it rains. You'll need it more on a sunny day.
lessons.Calendar.4.quiz.wrong: Not quite. The rain waters every tile by itself, so you can save your water for later. Try again.
lessons.Fishing.0.text: Fishing! Fish live in a pond, and you make the pond yourself. dig() digs a hole under the drone (plants won't grow there anymore, and plow() fills the hole back up with soil).
lessons.Fishing.1.text: An empty hole has no fish. Fill it with water: use(Goods.Water). waterLevel() shows how full the pond is: 1 means full. Pond water doesn't dry up.
lessons.Fishing.2.text: On a full pond, goFishing() casts the hook, waits a few seconds and catches a fish. It answers with the fish it caught, so you can keep it in a variable and compare it:
lessons.Fishing.3.text: But fish are shy. After a catch, the pond rests for a bit (it stops sparkling then), and goFishing() catches nothing. So to catch lots of fish, dig a few ponds and fish in them one by one.
lessons.Fishing.4.text: Fish are random, like rolling a die: Carp, often (+1 fish); Barbel, sometimes (+3); Ishkhan, the Lake Sevan trout, rarely (+10); Goldfish, very rarely (+50). And your first goldfish gets you a new hat!
lessons.Fishing.5.text: A question: the chance of a goldfish is 1%, which means 1 in 100. On average, how many times do you have to fish to catch one?
lessons.Fishing.5.quiz.right: Correct! 1 in 100 means about 100 casts on average. Sometimes you'll get lucky sooner, sometimes later.
lessons.Fishing.5.quiz.wrong: Not quite. 1% means about 1 time in 100 tries. So on average you need about 100 casts. Try again.
lessons.Fertilizer.0.text: Humus (Goods.Humus)! It comes all by itself, every 10 seconds.
lessons.Fertilizer.1.text: Now the soil can get tired. If you grow the same plant on the same tile again and again, the soil gets weak and the harvest shrinks, down to half. Tired soil looks paler.
lessons.Fertilizer.2.text: The soil gets a rest when you take turns with plants: eggplant one time, a different plant the next. Farmers call this crop rotation.
lessons.Fertilizer.3.text: And humus makes tired soil strong again right away, and gives a growing plant 2 seconds of growth:
lessons.Fertilizer.4.text: Think: how can you use whatsHere() to find out what was growing here, and then plant the other one?
lessons.Sunflowers.0.text: Pomegranates (Plants.Pomegranate)! A pomegranate grows in plowed soil and gives pomegranate juice (Goods.Juice).
lessons.Sunflowers.1.text: scan() counts a pomegranate's seeds: from 1 to 30. Only pomegranates with an even number of seeds give juice. An odd pomegranate gives no juice and even spills one.
lessons.Sunflowers.2.text: A number is even if dividing it by 2 leaves 0. The % sign gives you the remainder:
lessons.Sunflowers.2.code:
say(10 % 2);   // 0, so it's even
say(7 % 2);    // 1, so it's odd
lessons.Sunflowers.3.text: And now the coolest part: the combo! If each next even pomegranate has more seeds than the one before, the juice grows: 1, then 2, then 3… If the next one doesn't have more, the combo starts over from 1.
lessons.Sunflowers.4.text: For example, pomegranates with 4, 10 and 12 seeds give 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 juice, but the same pomegranates in the order 12, 10, 4 give only 1 + 1 + 1 = 3. Think: how can you find the even pomegranate with the fewest seeds?
lessons.Sunflowers.5.text: Juice does nothing on its own. With drink(), the drone drinks one juice and does its next 50 actions 2 times faster:
lessons.Sunflowers.6.text: Let's check. What will this code say?
lessons.Sunflowers.6.quiz.right: Correct! 18 divides by 2 with nothing left over, so 18 % 2 is 0 and the comparison is true. That's how we check if a number is even.
lessons.Sunflowers.6.quiz.wrong: Not quite. First work out 18 % 2 (the remainder when you divide by 2), then compare it with 0. Try again.
lessons.Cactus.0.text: Grapes (Plants.Grape)! Every grape has a sweetness from 0 to 9. scan() tells you the sweetness of the grape under the drone, and scan(Right) tells you its right neighbor's.
lessons.Cactus.1.text: Grapes love a tidy row. If the ripe grapes side by side in a row never get smaller from left to right (for example 1, 3, 3, 7), one gather() collects the whole row.
lessons.Cactus.2.text: A sorted row of n grapes gives n × n: 4 grapes give 16, and 8 give 64. In a row that isn't sorted, gather() collects only one grape.
lessons.Cactus.3.text: exchange() swaps the grape under the drone with the one next to it. It only works along a row, Right or Left:
lessons.Cactus.4.text: This is a real sorting problem, like in programming contests. Idea: compare a grape with its right neighbor, and if the left one is bigger, swap them. Think: how many times do you need to go along the row?
lessons.Debugger.0.text: Now there's a "Variables" window under "Storage". While your code is running or paused, it shows your variables and their values.
lessons.Debugger.1.text: Press the "Step" button to run your code one line at a time. That way you can watch the values change. Real programmers find bugs like this too.
lessons.Mazes.0.text: Mazes! You can sow a maze just like a plant. It covers the whole farm, and there's a treasure inside (Plants.Treasure).
lessons.Mazes.1.text: A maze costs magic dust: as much as the length of one side of the farm. Mushrooms give the dust. If you don't have enough, the maze will be smaller too.
lessons.Mazes.2.text: In a maze, scan() tells you where the treasure is, [x, y], and canGo() tells you if there's no wall on that side:
lessons.Mazes.3.text: Here's a secret: the "right-hand rule." If you always keep your right hand on the wall and keep walking, you'll find the treasure in the end.
lessons.Mazes.4.text: Gather the treasure with gather() and you'll get gold. And if you use the same amount of dust on the treasure again, it moves to a new spot, and you get even more gold.
lessons.Megafarm.0.text: Drone team! Now you can have more than one drone. newDrone() makes a new drone that runs the function you give it:
lessons.Megafarm.1.text: Careful: give newDrone() the function's name without (). The new drone starts on the tile where the drone that made it is standing. droneLimit() tells you the most drones you can have.
lessons.Megafarm.2.text: wait() waits for a drone to finish its work, then gives back its function's answer:
lessons.Dinosaurs.0.text: A snake! With wearHat(Hats.Snake) the drone turns into a snake, and a mouse (Plants.Mouse) shows up on the farm.
lessons.Dinosaurs.1.text: The snake hunts the mouse, but the mouse runs away: for every two snake steps, it moves one tile away. scan() tells you where the mouse is now:
lessons.Dinosaurs.2.text: Every mouse you catch makes the snake's tail longer. The snake can't cross its own tail or go past the edge of the farm. Tip: chase the mouse into a corner. From there it has nowhere to run.
lessons.Dinosaurs.3.text: When you switch to another hat, you get snake skin: the number of mice you caught times the snake's length.
reactions.Speed.0: Zoooom! The drone is faster now.
reactions.Grass.0: Wheat gives a bigger harvest now.
reactions.giantPumpkin.0: A giant watermelon! That's the biggest one I've ever seen!
reactions.pumpkinDied.0: Oh no, a watermelon waited too long and rotted. Plant a new one in its place, and next time gather sooner: when scan() is between 80 and 100.
reactions.mouseCaught.0: Got it! The snake's tail got longer. The next mouse is already here, and it's running too.
reactions.juiceNote.0: I've got news! Pomegranate juice doesn't drink itself anymore. To make the drone faster, write drink() in your code. One juice lasts for 50 actions.
reactions.idle.0: The drone hasn't done anything for a long time. Maybe the loop is empty, or the condition is never true.
reactions.helpIntro.1: I'm here! What do you want to know?
reactions.GoldenHat.0: The Golden hat! The drone is a real king now.
reactions.goldenFish.0: A goldfish! That's some rare luck!
reactions.goldenFish.1: Whoa, a goldfish! Keep it up!
reactions.Secret.0: You found the secret! Try wearHat(Hats.Secret).
quests.first_harvest.title: First harvest
quests.first_harvest.text: Write the command that gathers wheat and press ▶ "Run".
quests.first_harvest.hints.0: A command has three parts: a name, parentheses () and a semicolon ;.
quests.first_harvest.hints.1: The command that gathers wheat is called gather. Write it in the code window, on a new line below the comments.
quests.first_harvest.hints.2:
Step by step:
1) write the command's name: gather,
2) right after it: (),
3) at the end: ;,
4) press the green ▶ button.
If the line gets a red underline, check that every letter is an English letter.
quests.first_harvest.done: Hooray! You wrote your first code and gathered your first wheat. Look, it's in "Storage" now.
quests.hay_5.title: 5 wheat
quests.hay_5.text: Get 5 wheat. Press ▶ every time the wheat grows back.
quests.hay_5.hints.0: Wheat grows back in half a second. Press ▶ a few times.
quests.hay_5.hints.1: Each time you press ▶, the code runs once and the drone gathers 1 wheat.
quests.hay_5.hints.2: Press ▶, wait a moment, press ▶ again… until you have 5 wheat.
quests.hay_5.done: Great! But pressing ▶ forever gets boring, right? Let's fix that.
quests.buy_loops.title: Your first research
quests.buy_loops.text: Open "Research" and buy while for 5 wheat.
quests.buy_loops.hints.0: There's a "Research" button at the top. Press it.
quests.buy_loops.hints.1: The while card is at the very top of the tree. Press it, then press "Buy".
quests.buy_loops.hints.2: If the "Buy" button doesn't work, check that you have 5 wheat.
quests.buy_loops.done: You unlocked while! Now the drone can work without stopping.
quests.use_while.title: Nonstop work
quests.use_while.text: Write a while loop that gathers wheat again and again. Gather 20 more wheat.
quests.use_while.hints.0: A loop repeats the commands written inside its curly braces { }.
quests.use_while.hints.1: You need the word while, the condition true and the command that gathers wheat. Bridgy's lesson had an example with flip().
quests.use_while.hints.2:
Step by step:
1) write while,
2) in parentheses, write true,
3) open a curly brace {,
4) on a new line, write the gather command with ;,
5) close it with }.
Then press ▶.
quests.use_while.done: Way to go! The drone works on its own now. To stop the code, press "Stop".
quests.buy_speed.title: Faster
quests.buy_speed.text: Buy the "Speed" research. It's under the while card.
quests.buy_speed.hints.0: Open "Research". There are a few cards under while.
quests.buy_speed.hints.1: The Speed card has a fast drone on it. It costs 20 wheat.
quests.buy_speed.hints.2: If you don't have enough wheat, run your while loop and wait.
quests.buy_speed.done: Zoooom! The drone is faster now.
quests.buy_expand.title: Big farm
quests.buy_expand.text: Buy the "Big farm" research. The farm will grow, and you'll get the go() command.
quests.buy_expand.hints.2: Run your while loop, gather 30 wheat, then buy it.
quests.buy_expand.done: The farm got bigger! Now it's 2×2: 4 tiles.
quests.use_move.title: Farm tour
quests.use_move.text: Write code so the drone gathers wheat from several tiles: gather, go right, and so on forever. Gather 50 more wheat.
quests.use_move.hints.0: go(Right) moves the drone one tile to the right. From the last tile, it comes back to the first one.
quests.use_move.hints.1: You need a while (true) loop, gather() and go(Right). Inside a loop you can write several commands, one under the other.
quests.use_move.hints.2:
Step by step:
1) write an endless loop,
2) inside it, on the first line, gather the wheat,
3) on the second line, go right.
Each time around, the drone gathers one tile and moves on to the next.
quests.use_move.done: Perfect! Now the drone works all over the farm.
quests.buy_variables.title: Variables
quests.buy_variables.text: Buy the "a = 2" research. It unlocks variables.
quests.buy_variables.hints.2: If you don't have enough wheat, run your loop and wait.
quests.buy_variables.done: Variables remember values. They're one of the most important tools in programming.
quests.use_variables.title: Your first variable
quests.use_variables.text: Run code that has a variable (let) in it. For example, keep the direction the drone goes in a variable.
quests.use_variables.hints.0: You make a variable with the word let, a name and the = sign, for example: let side = Right.
quests.use_variables.hints.1: Write the variable's name where you used to write the value, for example inside the parentheses of go().
quests.use_variables.hints.2:
Step by step:
1) before the loop, make a variable and put a direction in it,
2) in the loop, write the variable's name inside the parentheses of go(),
3) run it and watch the drone go that way.
quests.use_variables.done: Nice one! Now you only have to change one line, and the drone goes a different way.
quests.buy_debug.title: Console
quests.buy_debug.text: Buy the say() research. It unlocks the say(), console.log() and alert() commands.
quests.buy_debug.hints.1: Check the price on the card: it only needs wheat.
quests.buy_debug.hints.2: Run your loop and wait until you have enough wheat.
quests.buy_debug.done: Now your code can talk to you!
quests.use_print.title: Tell me
quests.use_print.text: Run code that writes something in the console with say(). For example, show your variable.
quests.use_print.hints.0: Inside the parentheses of say(), write what you want to see: a number, text in quotes, or a variable's name.
quests.use_print.hints.1: The console is under the code window (on a phone, behind the console button).
quests.use_print.hints.2:
Step by step:
1) make a variable,
2) on the next line, write say, and inside the parentheses the variable's name,
3) run it and look at the console.
quests.use_print.done: See? say() is a programmer's best friend when something isn't working.
quests.buy_operators.title: Math
quests.buy_operators.text: Buy the "1 + 1" research. It unlocks math and comparing.
quests.buy_operators.hints.1: Check the price on the card: it only needs wheat.
quests.buy_operators.hints.2: If you're short on wheat, buy the "Wheat" research: it doubles your harvest.
quests.buy_operators.done: Now the drone can do math and compare, and you can write a for loop.
quests.buy_expand2.title: A 3×3 farm
quests.buy_expand2.text: Buy level 2 of "Big farm". The farm will become 3×3.
quests.buy_expand2.hints.0: Open the "Big farm" card and buy its second level.
quests.buy_expand2.hints.1: Check the price on the card: it only needs wheat.
quests.buy_expand2.hints.2: Run your loop and wait until you have enough wheat.
quests.whole_farm.title: The whole farm
quests.whole_farm.text: Write code so that in one run the drone visits every tile of the farm.
quests.whole_farm.hints.0: go(Right) moves the drone along a row, and go(Up) takes it up to the next row.
quests.whole_farm.hints.1: On a 3×3 farm, after going right 3 times, the drone is back at the start of its row. That's exactly the moment to go up one row.
quests.whole_farm.hints.2:
Step by step, inside an endless loop:
1) with a for loop, three times: gather and go right,
2) after the for loop, go up once.
Each time around covers one whole row.
quests.whole_farm.done: The drone covered the whole farm. Good plan!
quests.buy_senses.title: Where am I?
quests.buy_senses.text: Buy the "(x, y)" research so the drone knows where it is.
quests.buy_senses.hints.1: Check the price on the card: it only needs wheat.
quests.buy_senses.hints.2: Wheat is the fastest to gather, so let wheat grow on every tile.
quests.buy_senses.done: Now posX() and posY() tell you where the drone is.
quests.buy_plant.title: Time to sow
quests.buy_plant.text: Buy the sow() research. It unlocks rosehips and the if condition.
quests.buy_plant.hints.0: The sow() card is under "1 + 1". It also needs "Big farm".
quests.buy_plant.hints.1: Check the price on the card: it only needs wheat.
quests.buy_plant.hints.2: Run your loop and wait until you have enough wheat.
quests.buy_plant.done: Now you can plant rosehips. Rosehips give wood.
quests.wood_10.title: First wood
quests.wood_10.hints.0: A rosehip takes about 4 seconds to grow. Gather only ripe rosehips, or you'll get nothing.
quests.wood_10.hints.1: You need if, isRipe(), gather(), sow(Plants.Rosehip) and go(Right), inside a while loop.
quests.wood_10.hints.2:
Step by step, inside an endless loop:
1) use if to check: is it ripe?
2) if yes, gather it and plant a new rosehip right away (both inside the if's { }),
3) after the if, go right.
quests.wood_10.done: Here's your first wood! Wood buys lots of cool research.
quests.buy_lists.title: Lists
quests.buy_lists.hints.1: Check the price on the card: it needs wood.
quests.buy_lists.done: With lists, you can remember lots of values at once.
quests.buy_carrots.title: Eggplants
quests.buy_carrots.hints.0: The "Eggplant" card is under sow(). It opens after "[1, 2, 3]".
quests.buy_carrots.hints.1: Check the price on the card: it needs wood.
quests.buy_carrots.hints.2: Keep growing rosehips. A bigger farm fits more rosehips.
quests.buy_carrots.done: Eggplants! Remember: eggplants grow only on plowed soil, and you plant them from seeds.
quests.carrots_10.title: Eggplant harvest
quests.carrots_10.text: Gather wheat until seeds (Goods.Seeds) drop. Then plow the soil with plow(), plant eggplants (Plants.Eggplant) and gather 10 eggplants.
quests.carrots_10.hints.0: Seeds come from wheat: about 1 stalk in 20 drops one. You'll see "Seeds" in Storage. Every ripe eggplant also gives back 1–3 seeds.
quests.carrots_10.hints.1: plow() turns meadow into plowed soil. Plow each tile only once, or it turns back into meadow. You won't have many seeds at first, so leave a few tiles for wheat.
quests.carrots_10.hints.2:
Step by step:
1) first run a short program that plows a few tiles once,
2) then write a second program: in an endless loop, if the plant is ripe, gather it,
3) then try to plant an eggplant and go to the next tile.
Don't gather an eggplant before it's ripe, or you'll lose its seed.
quests.carrots_10.done: Yummy eggplants! You're a real farmer now.
quests.buy_watering.title: Water
quests.buy_watering.hints.1: Check the price on the card: it needs wood.
quests.buy_watering.hints.2: Grow rosehips so you have wood.
quests.buy_watering.done: Now you can water the soil.
quests.water_5.title: Wet soil
quests.water_5.text: Water the soil 5 times with use(Goods.Water).
quests.water_5.hints.0: Buckets of water pile up in "Storage" by themselves.
quests.water_5.hints.1: use(Goods.Water) waters the tile right under the drone. waterLevel() tells you how wet the soil is.
quests.water_5.hints.2:
Step by step:
1) in your plant loop, add a check: is waterLevel() less than 0.5?
2) if yes, water,
3) leave the rest as it was.
quests.water_5.done: Everything grows faster in wet soil.
quests.buy_calendar.title: Calendar
quests.buy_calendar.text: Buy the "Calendar" research. It's under sow().
quests.buy_calendar.hints.0: The "Calendar" card is under the sow() research.
quests.buy_calendar.hints.1: Check the price on the card: it needs wood and eggplants.
quests.buy_calendar.hints.2: Each season, grow whatever grows fast in that season. Check the TV button above the farm.
quests.buy_calendar.done: Now your code knows the season and the weather.
quests.season_code.title: Seasonal code
quests.season_code.text: Write code that checks the season with season() and does different things in different seasons.
quests.season_code.hints.0: season() returns Seasons.Spring, Seasons.Summer, Seasons.Autumn or Seasons.Winter.
quests.season_code.hints.1: Compare it with if: if (season() === Seasons.Winter) { … }.
quests.season_code.hints.2:
Step by step:
1) write if, and in the parentheses compare season() with one season,
2) inside { }, write what to do in that season,
3) inside else { }, write what to do in the other seasons,
4) run the code.
quests.season_code.done: Nice one! A good farmer always checks the calendar.
quests.repair_bridge.title: A bridge to the village
quests.repair_bridge.text: Open "Village" and fix the bridge: bring wood and wheat with the "Give" button.
quests.repair_bridge.hints.1: The bridge needs 300 wood and 500 wheat. You can bring them a little at a time.
quests.repair_bridge.hints.2: Write code so the drone gathers rosehips and wheat, then open the village and press "Give".
quests.repair_bridge.done: The bridge is ready! The villagers are coming back.
quests.first_request.title: Help a villager
quests.first_request.text: Complete one request from the village board.
quests.first_request.hints.0: The request board is in the village square.
quests.first_request.hints.1: Each request says what is needed and how much. Gather that much and press "Give".
quests.first_request.hints.2: New requests come every day, and you get a star for each one you complete.
quests.first_request.done: The villager is so happy! Save your stars for the village buildings.
quests.buy_trees.title: Apricot trees
quests.buy_trees.hints.1: Check the price on the card: it needs wood and eggplants.
quests.buy_trees.hints.2: Grow rosehips and eggplants at the same time, for example in different rows.
quests.buy_trees.done: Apricot trees give lots of wood, and every tree gives a harvest three times.
quests.trees_10.title: Forest keeper
quests.trees_10.hints.0: You plant an apricot tree with sow(Plants.ApricotTree). It doesn't disappear when you gather it, and it gives a harvest three times.
quests.trees_10.hints.1: scan() tells you how many harvests the tree has left. When it says 1, this is the last one, and after gathering you need to plant a new tree.
quests.trees_10.hints.2:
Step by step, inside an endless loop:
1) if the plant is ripe, first save what scan() says in a variable,
2) gather,
3) if the number you saved was 1, plant a new apricot tree (plant one on empty tiles too),
4) go to the next tile.
quests.buy_fertilizer.title: Humus
quests.buy_fertilizer.hints.1: Check the price on the card: it needs wood.
quests.buy_fertilizer.hints.2: Apricot trees give the most wood.
quests.buy_fertilizer.done: Humus makes the soil strong. But now the soil can get tired if you always grow the same plant.
quests.humus_5.title: Tired soil
quests.humus_5.text: Give the soil humus 5 times: use(Goods.Humus). Watch the pale, tired soil turn dark again.
quests.humus_5.hints.0: Humus piles up in "Storage" by itself. It helps both growing plants and tired soil.
quests.humus_5.hints.1: Soil gets tired when you harvest the same plant on the same tile again and again. To keep it fresh, take turns planting two different plants.
quests.humus_5.hints.2:
Step by step:
1) in your eggplant loop, use humus after planting a new plant,
2) to let the soil rest, use whatsHere() before you gather to find out what was growing there,
3) and plant the other plant.
quests.humus_5.done: Rested soil gives the full harvest. You really know your soil now!
quests.buy_fishing.title: Fishing
quests.buy_fishing.hints.1: Check the price on the card: it needs wood and eggplants.
quests.buy_fishing.hints.2: Gather the wood and eggplants you need, then open "Research" and buy the card.
quests.fill_pond.title: Pond
quests.fill_pond.text: Dig a pond and fill it with water until it's full.
quests.fill_pond.hints.0: You dig a pond with dig() and pour in water with use(Goods.Water).
quests.fill_pond.hints.1: waterLevel() tells you how full the pond is: 1 means full. You'll need a few buckets of water.
quests.fill_pond.hints.2:
The steps:
1) stand where you want the pond,
2) dig,
3) while the water level is less than 1, pour in water (while).
quests.fill_pond.done: The pond is full. The fish are already swimming!
quests.fish_20.title: First catch
quests.fish_20.hints.0: Stand on a full pond and fish with goFishing().
quests.fish_20.hints.1: One cast takes a few seconds, and then the pond rests a little. Repeat it in a loop, or dig a few more ponds.
quests.fish_20.hints.2:
The steps:
1) go to the pond,
2) write a loop that fishes again and again,
3) wait until you have 20 fish.
quests.golden_fish.title: Goldfish
quests.golden_fish.hints.0: A goldfish is very rare: about one in 100 casts. With lots of ponds, you'll catch one sooner.
quests.golden_fish.hints.1: goFishing() returns the fish it caught. Keep it in a variable and compare it with Fish.Goldfish.
quests.golden_fish.hints.2:
The steps:
1) fish and keep the fish in a variable,
2) repeat while it's not a goldfish (while and !==),
3) when you catch it, celebrate with say.
quests.golden_fish.done: A goldfiiish! And a new hat: the Fisher hat.
quests.repair_mill.title: Water mill
quests.repair_mill.hints.0: The mill needs wood, wheat, eggplants and 3 stars.
quests.repair_mill.hints.1: The villagers give you stars for their requests.
quests.repair_mill.hints.2: Complete all 3 of today's requests, and you'll get 2 more stars as a gift.
quests.make_flour.title: First flour
quests.make_flour.text: Build a mill on the farm and grind 5 flour.
quests.make_flour.hints.0: build(Machines.Mill) builds a mill under the drone.
quests.make_flour.hints.1: make(Goods.Flour) starts grinding, and gather() takes the finished flour.
quests.make_flour.hints.2:
Step by step:
1) stand on an empty tile and build a mill,
2) in a loop, check isRipe(), and if it's ready, gather,
3) then start grinding again.
quests.make_flour.done: What lovely flour! Now think about what you could bake with it.
quests.buy_utilities.text: Buy the "Math and random numbers" research.
quests.buy_utilities.hints.0: The card is under "[1, 2, 3]", and it says Math on it.
quests.buy_utilities.hints.1: Check the price on the card: it needs eggplants.
quests.buy_utilities.hints.2: For more eggplants, buy new levels of the "Eggplant" research and water the soil.
quests.buy_utilities.done: Now your code can get random numbers.
quests.buy_functions.title: Your own functions
quests.buy_functions.hints.1: Check the price on the card: it needs eggplants.
quests.buy_functions.done: Now you can make your own commands.
quests.use_functions.title: My first function
quests.use_functions.text: Make your own function with the word function, and call it.
quests.use_functions.hints.0: You make a function with the word function: function name() { … }, and you call it by its name: name().
quests.use_functions.hints.1: Think: which commands do you repeat a lot? For example, "gather and plant again" or "go along one row". Put them in a function.
quests.use_functions.hints.2:
Step by step:
1) write function, the function's name (English letters, no spaces) and (),
2) inside { }, write the commands,
3) outside the function, call it by its name and ().
quests.use_functions.done: Great function! Functions make code short and easy to understand.
quests.buy_pumpkins.title: Watermelons
quests.buy_pumpkins.hints.0: The "Watermelons" card is under "Apricot trees". It opens after "function f()".
quests.buy_pumpkins.hints.1: Check the price on the card: it needs wood and eggplants.
quests.buy_pumpkins.hints.2: Apricot trees give lots of wood, and the next levels of the "Eggplant" research give more eggplants.
quests.buy_pumpkins.done: Watermelons! You have to gather them at just the right moment: not too early, not too late.
quests.melon_10.title: Sweet watermelon
quests.melon_10.text: Gather 10 watermelons. Gather a watermelon when its sweetness (scan()) is 80 or more.
quests.melon_10.hints.0: A watermelon (Plants.Watermelon) is planted on plowed soil and costs eggplants. After it grows, it gets sweeter for a few seconds.
quests.melon_10.hints.1: scan() gives the sweetness, from 0 to 100. Gathered below 80, it gives nothing, and a little after 100 the watermelon rots.
quests.melon_10.hints.2:
Step by step, inside an endless loop:
1) use if to check: is scan() greater than or equal to 80?
2) if yes, gather,
3) then try to plant a new watermelon (it works in a rotten one's place too) and go to the next tile.
If your watermelons rot, plant on fewer tiles.
quests.melon_10.done: Sweet! You learned to use a number to decide when to gather.
quests.buy_sunflowers.title: Pomegranates
quests.buy_sunflowers.hints.1: Check the price on the card: it needs eggplants.
quests.buy_sunflowers.hints.2: For more eggplants, buy new levels of the "Eggplant" research.
quests.buy_sunflowers.done: Pomegranates give pomegranate juice, and with drink() the juice makes the drone faster.
quests.power_10.title: Pomegranate juice
quests.power_10.text: Gather 10 pomegranate juice. Only pomegranates with an even number of seeds give juice.
quests.power_10.hints.0: A pomegranate (Plants.Pomegranate) is planted on plowed soil and costs 1 eggplant. scan() counts its seeds.
quests.power_10.hints.1: A number is even if % 2 gives 0. Don't gather an odd pomegranate with gather(): it spills juice. To get rid of it, you can plow its tile twice.
quests.power_10.hints.2:
Idea, inside an endless loop:
1) if the pomegranate is ripe, find out its number of seeds with scan(),
2) if it's even, gather it; if not, plow twice,
3) plant a new pomegranate and go to the next tile.
For more juice, gather the even pomegranates from smallest to biggest.
quests.power_10.done: Tasty juice! And pomegranates gathered from smallest to biggest give more and more.
quests.drink_juice.title: Fast drone
quests.drink_juice.text: Run code where the drone drinks pomegranate juice: drink().
quests.drink_juice.hints.0: drink() uses up one juice and makes the drone faster for its next 50 actions.
quests.drink_juice.hints.1: So the juice isn't wasted, first check that you have some: count(Goods.Juice) tells you how much.
quests.drink_juice.hints.2:
Step by step:
1) at the start of your longest loop, use if to check: do you have juice?
2) if yes, call drink(),
3) count the actions with a variable, and drink again after every 50.
quests.drink_juice.done: Zoooom! With juice, the drone flies twice as fast.
quests.buy_mulberry.title: Mulberry tree
quests.buy_mulberry.hints.0: The card is under "Apricot trees". It also needs the "(x, y)" research.
quests.buy_mulberry.hints.1: Check the price on the card: it needs wood and eggplants.
quests.buy_mulberry.hints.2: Apricot trees give lots of wood, and eggplants grow fast in watered soil.
quests.buy_mulberry.done: Mulberry trees and rosehips are good neighbors. The bees will help!
quests.mulberry_10.title: Help from the bees
quests.mulberry_10.text: Harvest 10 mulberry trees. Try to have a ripe rosehip next to every mulberry tree: then the wood is doubled.
quests.mulberry_10.hints.0: You plant a mulberry tree with sow(Plants.MulberryTree). If a tile next to it has a ripe rosehip when you gather, you get 2 times more wood.
quests.mulberry_10.hints.1: Plant like a chessboard: mulberry, rosehip, mulberry… When two tiles are side by side, one has an even x + y and the other an odd one.
quests.mulberry_10.hints.2:
Step by step:
1) use (posX() + posY()) % 2 to decide: is this a mulberry tile or a rosehip tile?
2) on a mulberry tile, gather the ripe tree and plant it again,
3) on a rosehip tile, only plant if it's empty, and don't gather: the bees need the ripe rosehip.
quests.mulberry_10.done: Bzzzz! The bees are happy, and so are you.
quests.buy_mushrooms.title: Mushrooms
quests.buy_mushrooms.text: Buy the "Mushrooms" research. It needs fish.
quests.buy_mushrooms.hints.0: The card is under "Watering". It opens after "Math and random numbers".
quests.buy_mushrooms.hints.1: It needs fish and watermelons. Check the price on the card.
quests.buy_mushrooms.hints.2: If you're short on fish, dig a few ponds and write code that fishes in all of them, one by one.
quests.buy_mushrooms.done: The mushrooms are waiting for you. But careful, they're sneaky!
quests.mushrooms_10.title: Sneaky mushroom
quests.mushrooms_10.text: Gather 10 mushrooms. If a mushroom guesses which way you'll look, it runs away.
quests.mushrooms_10.hints.0: Plant a mushroom and wait until it's ripe. Then tell gather() which way to look: Right or Left.
quests.mushrooms_10.hints.1: If you always pick the same thing, the mushroom will learn. Your choice has to be random every time. Remember Math.random().
quests.mushrooms_10.hints.2:
The steps:
1) get a random number from 0 to 1,
2) if it's less than 0.5, look one way; if not, look the other way,
3) then plant again.
quests.mushrooms_10.done: Way to go! You beat the mushroom with randomness.
quests.buy_mazes.title: Garden maze
quests.buy_mazes.hints.0: The card is under "Mushrooms". It opens after "function f()".
quests.buy_mazes.hints.1: It needs magic dust. Check the price on the card.
quests.buy_mazes.hints.2: Mushrooms give magic dust. For more dust, buy new levels of "Mushrooms".
quests.buy_mazes.done: There's gold hidden in the garden maze.
quests.maze_gold.title: Treasure
quests.maze_gold.text: Find the treasure in the maze and gather 100 gold.
quests.maze_gold.hints.0: Plant a maze: sow(Plants.Maze). It needs magic dust.
quests.maze_gold.hints.1: scan() gives the treasure's position, and canGo() tells you if there's a wall. The right-hand rule always works.
quests.maze_gold.hints.2:
The right-hand rule:
1) keep the direction in a variable (with a list of directions: [Up, Right, Down, Left]),
2) at every step, first try to turn right; if you can't, go straight; if you can't do that either, turn left,
3) when you reach the treasure, gather().
quests.buy_yellow_melon.title: Yellow watermelon
quests.buy_yellow_melon.hints.1: It needs watermelons. Check the price on the card.
quests.buy_yellow_melon.hints.2: For more watermelons, buy new levels of "Watermelons" and gather them at the right moment.
quests.buy_yellow_melon.done: Yellow watermelons spread on their own. All you have to do is gather them at the right moment.
quests.yellow_100.title: Watermelon field
quests.yellow_100.text: Gather 100 yellow watermelons. Remember: n ripe watermelons touching each other give n × n together.
quests.yellow_100.hints.0: A yellow watermelon (Plants.YellowMelon) is planted on plowed soil. A ripe one sends out tendrils to the empty plowed soil next to it.
quests.yellow_100.hints.1: Planting just one and waiting is enough. flip() is handy for waiting: each flip takes one second.
quests.yellow_100.hints.2:
Step by step:
1) plow part of the farm once and clear the plants off it,
2) plant one yellow watermelon,
3) do a few dozen flips with a for loop so the field grows,
4) gather and see how many you got. Try waiting longer.
quests.yellow_100.done: A whole field with one command! Square numbers grow fast.
quests.buy_square_melon.title: Square watermelon
quests.buy_square_melon.hints.1: It needs watermelons. Check the price on the card.
quests.buy_square_melon.done: Square watermelons love to join up into a giant.
quests.giant_pumpkin.title: Giant watermelon
quests.giant_pumpkin.text: Grow and gather a giant square watermelon (at least 2×2).
quests.giant_pumpkin.hints.0: If 4 square watermelons (Plants.SquareMelon) ripen side by side and make a square, they join together.
quests.giant_pumpkin.hints.1: Don't gather any of them until they're all ripe. The giant is one big watermelon spread over several tiles.
quests.giant_pumpkin.hints.2: Plant square watermelons on a 2×2 patch, wait until they join, and gather it with one gather().
quests.giant_pumpkin.done: A giant watermelon! The bigger the watermelon, the bigger the harvest.
quests.big_pumpkin.title: The biggest watermelon
quests.big_pumpkin.text: Gather a giant square watermelon at least 3×3 in size.
quests.big_pumpkin.hints.0: A 3×3 giant gives 27 watermelons instead of 9 separate ones.
quests.big_pumpkin.hints.1: Plant on all 9 tiles and don't gather until they join. Two for loops, one inside the other, help you go over the square.
quests.big_pumpkin.hints.2:
Idea:
1) plant a 3×3 square with two for loops,
2) wait a few seconds (with flips, for example),
3) gather on any tile of the giant.
quests.big_pumpkin.done: Whoa, what a giant watermelon! You're an amazing farmer.
quests.buy_objects.title: Objects
quests.buy_objects.hints.1: It needs watermelons. Check the price on the card.
quests.buy_objects.done: In an object, every value has its own name. That's really handy.
quests.buy_cactus.title: Grapevines
quests.buy_cactus.hints.0: The card is under "Watermelons". It opens after "{a: 1}".
quests.buy_cactus.hints.1: It needs all three kinds of watermelon. Check the price on the card.
quests.buy_cactus.hints.2: Let the yellow watermelons grow into a big field, and the square ones into a big giant. The bigger, the better.
quests.buy_cactus.done: The grapevines want you to put them in order.
quests.cactus_chain.title: A row of grapes
quests.cactus_chain.text: Gather a sorted row of at least 5 grapes with one gather().
quests.cactus_chain.hints.0: Sorted means that, from left to right, the grapes never get smaller anywhere in the row, for example: 1, 3, 3, 7, 9.
quests.cactus_chain.hints.1: Compare a grape with its right neighbor: scan() > scan(Right), and if so, exchange(Right). One pass isn't enough: repeat it as many times as there are grapes in the row.
quests.cactus_chain.hints.2:
Idea (bubble sort):
1) plant grapes on 5 tiles of one row and wait until they're ripe,
2) go along the row; on each tile, compare with the right neighbor and swap them if the left one is bigger,
3) repeat the pass 5 times,
4) at the end, one gather().
quests.cactus_chain.done: A real sorting algorithm! You're awesome.
quests.buy_megafarm.title: Drone team
quests.buy_megafarm.hints.1: Check the price on the card: it needs gold.
quests.buy_megafarm.hints.2: If you move the treasure (by using the same amount of dust on the treasure), you can get gold from the same maze again.
quests.buy_megafarm.done: Now several drones can work together.
quests.use_drones.title: Teamwork
quests.use_drones.text: Run code that makes a new drone with newDrone().
quests.use_drones.hints.0: newDrone() needs a function for the new drone to run.
quests.use_drones.hints.1: Write the function separately, and give newDrone() its name, without ().
quests.use_drones.hints.2:
Step by step:
1) write a function that farms one row,
2) make a few drones with a loop (one less than droneLimit()), going up one row each time,
3) at the end, call the same function for the main drone too.
quests.use_drones.done: A drone team! Together they're much faster.
quests.buy_dinosaurs.title: Snake
quests.buy_dinosaurs.hints.1: It needs grapes. Check the price on the card.
quests.buy_dinosaurs.hints.2: Long sorted rows of grapes give the most grapes.
quests.buy_dinosaurs.done: Sssss! The drone can turn into a snake.
quests.bones_100.title: Snake skin
quests.bones_100.text: Get 100 snake skin by catching mice with the snake.
quests.bones_100.hints.0: You get snake skin when you take off the snake hat: the number of mice caught times the snake's length.
quests.bones_100.hints.1: scan() tells you where the mouse is. The mouse runs away, so ask again before every step. In a corner, it has nowhere to run.
quests.bones_100.hints.2:
Idea:
1) put on the snake hat,
2) in a loop, each time find the mouse's [x, y] with scan() and take one step toward it,
3) after a few mice, change your hat and get the snake skin.
quests.final.title: Golden farm
quests.final.hints.1: You need lots of snake skin and gold. Use many drones and big mazes.
quests.final.hints.2: Buy new levels of the "Drone team", "Garden maze" and "Snake" research to multiply your harvest.
credits.0.text: Hooray! You've unlocked the whole research tree!
credits.1.text: You learned loops, conditions, variables, functions, lists, objects, sorting and how to find your way through mazes. That's the path of a real programmer.
credits.2.text: Bridgy is super proud of you. You can keep playing and write even faster code. Thanks for playing Bridgy's Farm!
